clue.text: As she and I, periodically getting stuck in Circle Line ...

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter of the words is kept
something stuck in another thing ends up lodged inside it, enclosed on both sides

blocks.note: an arc is a curved line forming part of a circle; its first two letters come first
the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the phrase
the last letter of the arc closes around the inserted letters

explanation.surface: A couple of travellers keep getting stranded on London's Circle Line, the ellipsis leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: ARC (a circle line) wraps around SENI to give ARSENIC. 'As' is not a link word at the start: it is the chemical symbol, and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The element arsenic has the chemical symbol As in the periodic table, which the word periodically also hints at.

clue.text: This compiler is able to support a father from the continent

indicators.note: in a down clue something that supports another sits beneath it, so these letters follow the earlier ones

blocks.note: taken as written
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the setter refers to themself as I
can means is able

explanation.surface: The setter is able to support a father who comes from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter calling themself 'this compiler' is a crossword habit for I.
explanation.definitionFit: African means coming from Africa, and 'the continent' here is that large landmass, not mainland Europe as Britons usually mean.

clue.text: Playing My Sonny Boy for lad?

indicators.note: playing a tune can mean playing around with it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone plays the old song Sonny Boy, perhaps in honour of a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sonny Boy' looks like the song title, but the fodder stops at Sonny and Boy starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym is a word with the same meaning as another, as boy shares its meaning with lad.

clue.text: Hot toddy, say, stocked by Rising Sun

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means going upwards, so the word is read bottom to top
goods stocked by a shop are held inside it, so the word sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
e.g., for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A pub called the Rising Sun keeps hot toddies on its menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising Sun' looks like a pub name; Rising reverses SUN to NUS, which then holds EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus is a hot drink of port or sherry with sugar, lemon and spice, much like a toddy.

clue.text: Dean runs fitness centre, spotless on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means wrapping round, so the word surrounds the others

blocks.note: spotless means clean
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a gym is a fitness centre

explanation.surface: A man called Dean runs a spotlessly clean gym.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean looks like a first name, but it is a church title.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior cleric in charge of a cathedral or chapter, so he is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: ... leaves causing problems down the line?

definitions.text: leaves causing problems down the line?

blocks.clueFragment: leaves causing problems down the line
blocks.note: surface reading: someone leaving a railway line, carrying on from the Circle Line in the previous clue, causes delays

blocks.clueFragment: leaves causing problems down the line
blocks.note: setter's reading: dried plant leaves that are smoked and cause health trouble years later

explanation.surface: Continuing the Circle Line story, someone's departure causes disruption further along the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb and 'the line' like a railway; read leaves as plant foliage and down the line as in the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is a plant whose cured foliage is smoked, and smoking brings illnesses such as cancer much later in life.

clue.text: Row about minute recording device

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes around the next

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
standard abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a minute-taking machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Row reads as a quarrel; it is a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A timer is a gadget that measures and records how much time passes.

clue.text: According to Spooner, Mrs Johnson ordered security fence

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, which the solver must do here

blocks.note: Mrs Johnson is Carrie, wife of former UK prime minister Boris Johnson, and ordered is bade; swap the opening sounds of Carrie bade

explanation.surface: The prime minister's wife demanded a security fence.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of Carrie bade gives Barry cade.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a makeshift barrier put up to block a road or keep people out.

clue.text: Fellow unwrapped eat-in flatbread

indicators.note: unwrapped means with the wrapping off, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: a chap is a fellow
the phrase with its first and last letters taken off

explanation.surface: A man unwraps a flatbread to eat in rather than take away.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened round bread from South Asia, cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: Instrument first to observe constellation

indicators.note: first to points to the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: first letter of observe
Carina, the Keel, is a southern constellation

explanation.surface: An astronomer's instrument is used first to observe a constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a telescope; the instrument is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, so it plays music.

clue.text: Republican O'Neill famously returned to apostatise

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the name is read from end to start

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for Republican
Eugene O'Neill was the famous American playwright

explanation.surface: An Irish republican figure called O'Neill famously went back on his allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an Irish politician; the famous O'Neill is the playwright Eugene, whose first name is read backwards after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Renegue is an old spelling of renege, meaning to abandon one's faith or principles, which is what an apostate does.

clue.text: Wine bar with regular servings of paella

indicators.note: regular servings are helpings at even intervals, so every second letter of the dish is taken

blocks.note: a Mars bar is a well-known chocolate bar
the second, fourth and sixth letters of paella

explanation.surface: A tapas bar pairs its wine with small portions of paella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wine bar' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Wine'; the bar is a chocolate one.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified dessert wine from Sicily, so it is a specific example of the general term.

clue.text: Sticky sweet stuff?

blocks.note: surface reading: something gooey and sugary such as toffee or syrup
setter's reading: sweet stuff that comes from a stick, the tall stalk of a plant

explanation.walkthrough: Sticky usually means gluey; here it means coming from a stick-like stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweetener is extracted from the juice of a tall grass whose stems look like walking sticks.

clue.text: Arab discovered viral quiz programme

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so the outer letters of the word are dropped

blocks.note: the word with its first and last letters stripped away
QI is a long-running BBC television quiz show

explanation.surface: An Arab contestant was spotted on a quiz show that went viral online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' seems to mean found, but it means uncovered. QI is a British panel quiz programme hosted by Stephen Fry and later Sandi Toksvig.
explanation.definitionFit: Most people of that Middle Eastern country are Arabs, so a citizen of it is an Arab by nationality.

clue.text: Young maiden has my back in Nag's Head pub

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Nag's is used
back means turned round, so the little word is read the other way
in places the turned word inside the surrounding letters

blocks.note: first letter of Nag's
taken as written
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A girl goes back to her local, the Nag's Head pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nag's Head looks like a pub name, but Head only means the first letter of Nag's; 'pub' does the real pub work.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth a nymph is a beautiful young female spirit, and the word is also used loosely for a girl.

clue.text: Ivory polisher turning eighty admits revolting offence

indicators.note: turning means changing form, so the number's letters are rearranged
admits means lets in, so the jumbled letters hold another word inside
revolting is read as revolving, turning the word round to run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: An elderly antiques polisher of eighty confesses to a disgusting crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivories is slang for teeth, so the ivory polisher works in dentistry, not antiques.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental hygienist cleans and polishes patients' teeth, and teeth are jokingly called ivories.

clue.text: Mrs Simpson & Ms Hayworth drop ecstasy downing a cocktail

indicators.note: to drop something is to leave it out, so a letter is removed from the first name
downing means swallowing, so the names take the next letter inside them

blocks.note: Marge Simpson is Homer's wife in The Simpsons
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written
Rita Hayworth was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: Two famous women give up drugs and knock back a drink instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first woman loses the drug; the second name stays whole, and the pair together swallow the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a mixed drink of tequila, lime juice and orange liqueur served in a salt-rimmed glass.

clue.text: Entertaining character with interesting relations?

blocks.note: surface reading: a fun person with a colourful family
setter's reading: relations are things related, that is told, so this is someone who tells good stories

explanation.walkthrough: Relations looks like relatives; here it means narrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, someone who amuses company with stories.

clue.text: Ideal for broadcasting etc, Nigel Farage finally gets a break

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the surname
a break smashes things, so the collected letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
last letter of Farage

explanation.surface: A politician who seems made for television finally gets his big break.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage is a British populist politician; only his first name and the last letter of his surname feed the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone telegenic looks good and comes across well on television, so they suit being shown on air.

clue.text: Little stick for young swimmer

blocks.note: a tad is a little bit
a pole is a long stick

explanation.surface: A child learning to swim holds a small stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval stage of a frog or toad, living and moving in water before growing legs.

clue.text: Ramble on in English, a bit like some popes?

indicators.note: a bit means a part, so the answer is a stretch of the clue's own letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone rambles on in English, rather like certain long-winded popes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside rambLE ON IN English. Thirteen popes took the name Leo.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means relating to a Pope Leo, as well as lion-like, so it describes popes of that name.

clue.text: Moderate Liberal support for the arts?

blocks.note: to ease is to moderate or lessen
standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A moderate Liberal politician backs public funding for the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like arts funding policy, but the support is a physical one for a painter's canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds a painter's canvas upright, literally propping up artistic work.

clue.text: Southern Feds drafted into Alien Section

indicators.note: agents drafted into a unit are placed inside it, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for southern
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film
G-men are US government agents, as are Feds

explanation.surface: Southern FBI agents are called in to an alien-investigation section.
explanation.walkthrough: Alien Section sounds like a government department; Section alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one of the parts into which something is divided, so it is a portion or division.

clue.text: Doctor gently accepting husband is tedious

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order
accepting means taking in, so the jumbled letters take a letter inside

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A doctor who gently takes in a woman's husband finds him boring.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a person; it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthy means going on for a long time, and something drawn out is wearisome and dull.

clue.text: Finished keeping queen bee

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the first word holds the next inside it

blocks.note: done means finished
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A beekeeper has finished looking after the hive's queen bee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen bee' looks like one phrase; queen is R in the wordplay and bee alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male honeybee, whose role is to mate with the queen rather than gather nectar.

clue.text: Ring footballer's missus about trending topic

blocks.note: a ring is a band, as in a wedding band
WAGs, wives and girlfriends, is British slang for footballers' partners
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone phones a footballer's wife to chat about what is currently trending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb meaning phone, but it gives BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandwagon is a fashionable cause or craze that many people suddenly join, as in jumping on the bandwagon.

clue.text: A darkly romantic man, Corbyn lost his head, sadly

indicators.note: losing a head means losing the top, so the first letter of the name goes
sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: Jeremy Corbyn, former leader of the UK Labour Party

explanation.surface: Jeremy Corbyn, a gloomy idealist, sadly lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Corbyn without C is rearranged. Lord Byron was the Romantic poet famed as mad, bad and dangerous to know.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron was a leading English Romantic poet whose brooding heroes gave rise to the term Byronic.

clue.text: Squeeze current out of cables

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so a letter is taken away from the following word

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
wiring is a system of electrical cables

explanation.surface: An electrician squeezes the current out of the cables.
explanation.definitionFit: To wring is to twist and compress something hard, as when wringing out wet laundry.

clue.text: Musical featuring Italy's premier actor

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of Italy is used
a show featuring something includes it, so the show's name holds the letter

blocks.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Oliver Twist
first letter of Italy

explanation.surface: A musical starring Italy's leading actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier actor' reads as a phrase; premier belongs to the wordplay and actor alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was among the most celebrated stage and film performers of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Famous rapper fails to finish Bible books

indicators.note: failing to finish leaves the end undone, so the final letter of the name is dropped

blocks.note: Eminem is the American rap star
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A famous rapper never gets to the end of reading the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent describes someone distinguished and well known in their field, so it matches renowned or celebrated.

clue.text: Turn out old northern football team

blocks.note: to evert is to turn inside out
standard abbreviation for old
standard abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: An old northern football team turns out to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the rare verb evert. Everton is a Liverpool club in English football's top flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a professional soccer club based in Liverpool in the north-west of England.

clue.text: Gently changing sides initially in a fitting manner

indicators.note: changing sides swaps left for right, and initially says this happens at the very first letter

blocks.note: lightly means gently, with little force

explanation.surface: Gently swapping sides at the start seems the proper thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: L for left at the start of LIGHTLY becomes R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Rightly means correctly or properly, which is to say in a way that is appropriate or justified.
